For assumptions, I'll flag that the flag change wasn't logged as a formal change event, there's no clear deploy window, and the ZeroDivisionError linked to the spend-summary path is inferred from logs — the recovery tied to the flag revert is correlation, not confirmed causation, and the underlying defect likely remains unresolved. assumptions: The flag change at 23:25 is taken as the trigger from log evidence and the flag provider's change history; no separate audit record of who made the change or why was reviewed.
Causation is inferred from correlation: the error signature appeared at the flag flip and cleared after the revert. The defect itself was not reproduced or tested during the incident.
No production deploy was found in the 24-hour change window, so the alternative 'bad deployment' explanation was ruled out on the strength of that empty window alone.

The defect in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:35 is assumed to be still present in the codebase; reverting the flag restored service but did not fix the code, so re-enabling the flag before the pull request lands would likely reproduce the incident.
Impact is assumed limited to account-page requests, since only that endpoint appears in the error logs; no direct check of checkout or other flows was performed.
Only this service's own logs and metrics were examined; no downstream or client-side confirmation of user-visible impact was gathered.
The recovery timestamp is taken from the service's own metrics returning to baseline, not from independent confirmation that shoppers could load the page.
input.executive_summary: For roughly six minutes late on 22 September 2026 (23:25 to 23:31 UTC), shoppers loading their account page on the online shop were likely to get an error instead of the page. Nothing else about the shop was affected, and no data was lost or corrupted. The cause was a configuration switch that sent account-page traffic down a newer code path containing a bug; the switch was put back to its previous setting, and the account page returned to its normal behaviour immediately. A draft code change has been opened to fix the underlying bug so the newer path can be enabled safely in future. Automated response handling from alert to mitigation took well under a minute; the bulk of the customer impact happened before the alert fired.
input.root_cause: The feature flag `legacy-checkout-fallback` was switched from on to off at 23:25 UTC, which routed account-page traffic off the legacy path and onto the new spend-summary code, where an unguarded division raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:35. The flag flip exposed a latent defect rather than introducing one: no deploy or release appears in the 24 hours before onset, and the error signature in the logs changes from incidental ClientDisconnected to ZeroDivisionError exactly at the minute the flag partially rolled off, then worsens as it went fully off.
